title: Temperature dependence of resistance-in-series parameters during ultrafiltration of milk protein concentrate

record.title: Temperature dependence of resistance-in-series parameters during ultrafiltration of milk protein concentrate
record.abstract: The resistance-in-series model was applied to cross-flow ultrafiltration of milk protein concentrate (MPC-80) at temperatures of 10, 20, 30, and 40 °C using a 50 kDa regenerated cellulose membrane. Intrinsic membrane resistance, reversible fouling resistance, and irreversible fouling resistance were quantified after 2-hour filtration runs at 2 bar TMP and a feed velocity of 0.5 m/s. Membrane resistance was temperature-independent at 1.8 × 10¹² m⁻¹, consistent with viscosity correction. Reversible fouling resistance decreased from 6.1 × 10¹² m⁻¹ at 10 °C to 2.7 × 10¹² m⁻¹ at 40 °C, attributed to reduced protein–protein interactions at higher temperature. However, irreversible fouling resistance increased above 35 °C, likely due to thermal denaturation and irreversible protein adsorption. An optimal operating temperature window of 25–32 °C was identified that balances low viscosity with acceptable irreversible fouling. These findings are relevant to CIP scheduling and inter-run flux restoration.
